doc_description: Comprehensive Johnson & Johnson Q4 and full-year 2022 earnings release summarizing $23.7B Q4 and $94.9B FY sales amid significant FX headwinds and lower COVID-19 vaccine revenue, adjusted EPS of $2.35 (Q4) and $10.15 (FY), detailed regional and segment breakouts with extensive GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliations, notable MedTech/Pharma updates, and full-year 2023 adjusted sales/EPS guidance excluding the COVID-19 vaccine, with webcast and forward-looking disclosures.

structure.title: OVERALL FINANCIAL RESULTS
structure.heading: 1 OVERALL FINANCIAL RESULTS
structure.start_phrase: Note: values may have been rounded
structure.summary:
- Johnson & Johnson issued a press release detailing Q4 and full-year 2022 results and 2023 guidance.
- Q4 2022:
  - Reported sales declined 4.4% to $23.7B, primarily due to unfavorable foreign exchange and lower COVID-19 vaccine sales; operational growth excluding COVID-19 vaccine was +4.6%.
  - EPS fell 24.9% to $1.33; adjusted EPS rose 10.3% to $2.35.
- Full-year 2022:
  - Reported sales grew 1.3% to $94.9B, with operational growth of 6.1%, reflecting strong commercial execution partially offset by FX headwinds.
  - EPS decreased 13.8% to $6.73; adjusted EPS increased 3.6% to $10.15.
- 2023 guidance:
  - Adjusted operational sales growth excluding COVID-19 vaccine of 4.0%.
  - Adjusted operational EPS of $10.50, implying 3.5% growth.
- CEO commentary emphasized the strength and stability of all three business segments amid macroeconomic challenges and confidence in near-term growth and long-term value creation.
- Overall financial metrics (select):
  - Q4: Net earnings $3.52B; adjusted net earnings $6.22B.
  - FY: Net earnings $17.94B; adjusted net earnings $27.04B.
- Regional performance:
  - Q4: U.S. sales +2.9%; International -11.5% reported, with significant FX drag; worldwide -4.4% reported, +0.9% operational.
  - FY: U.S. +3.0% reported; International -0.6% reported but +9.1% operational; worldwide +1.3% reported, +6.1% operational.
- Segment performance (Q4):
  - Consumer Health: +1.0% reported, +6.4% operational.
  - Pharmaceutical: -7.4% reported, -2.5% operational (FX a major headwind).
  - MedTech: -1.2% reported, +4.9% operational.
- Non-GAAP notes: “Operational” excludes translational currency; “Adjusted operational” also excludes net M&A impacts; adjusted earnings exclude intangible amortization and special items.

nodes.title: Consumer Health
nodes.heading: 4.1 Consumer Health
nodes.start_phrase:
Consumer Health worldwide adjusted operational sales increased 3.9%* predominately driven by over -the-
counter (OTC) products .
nodes.summary:
- Full-year 2022 vs. 2021 results show modest reported growth overall, with stronger underlying (non-GAAP) operational performance and a significant negative currency impact.
- Worldwide sales were $94.9B (up 1.3% reported; +6.1% operational; currency −4.8%; +6.2% adjusted operational).
- Segment sales:
  - Consumer Health: $15.0B (down 0.5% reported; +3.9% adjusted operational).
  - Pharmaceutical: $52.6B (up 1.7% reported; +6.8% adjusted operational).
  - MedTech: $27.4B (up 1.4% reported; +6.1% adjusted operational).
- Consumer Health adjusted operational growth was driven by OTC products—especially TYLENOL and MOTRIN analgesics, upper respiratory, and digestive health in international markets—and Skin Health/Beauty led by NEUTROGENA outside the U.S.; partially offset by weaker Oral Care internationally.
- Pharmaceutical adjusted operational growth was led by DARZALEX, STELARA, ERLEADA, TREMFYA, and INVEGA long-acting injectables; partially offset by declines in REMICADE, IMBRUVICA, and ZYTIGA.
- Notes/definitions: figures use non-GAAP operational and adjusted operational metrics (excluding translational currency and, for adjusted, M&A effects); certain international OTC products (primarily in China) were reclassified from Pharmaceutical to Consumer Health; values may be rounded.

nodes.title: Pharmaceutical
nodes.heading: 4.2 Pharmaceutical
nodes.start_phrase: Pharmaceutical worldwide adjusted operational sales grew 6.8%*, driven by DARZALEX (daratumumab), a biologic for the treatment of multiple myeloma, STELARA (ustekinumab), a biologic for the treatment of a number of immune -mediated inflammatory diseases,
nodes.summary:
- Overview of Johnson & Johnson’s full-year 2022 results versus 2021, with worldwide sales of $94.9B (+1.3% reported; +6.2% adjusted operational), and segment performance:
  - Consumer Health: $15.0B (-0.5% reported; +3.9% adjusted operational)
  - Pharmaceutical: $52.6B (+1.7% reported; +6.8% adjusted operational)
  - MedTech: $27.4B (+1.4% reported; +6.1% adjusted operational)
  - Notes clarify non-GAAP measures, exclusions for currency and M&A, and a reclassification of certain international OTC products from Pharmaceutical to Consumer Health.

- Segment commentary on growth drivers and headwinds:
  - Consumer Health: Growth led by OTC (TYLENOL, MOTRIN, upper respiratory, digestive health) and NEUTROGENA outside the U.S.; partially offset by international Oral Care softness.
  - Pharmaceutical: Growth driven by DARZALEX, STELARA, ERLEADA, TREMFYA, and long-acting INVEGA formulations; partially offset by declines in REMICADE, IMBRUVICA, and ZYTIGA.
  - MedTech: Strength in electrophysiology (Interventional Solutions), contact lenses (Vision), and wound closure (General Surgery).

- Notable quarterly announcements:
  - Regulatory: FDA clearance for DePuy Synthes TELIGEN System; FDA approval of TECVAYLI (teclistamab-cqyv) for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma; BLA submitted to FDA for talquetamab in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.
  - Clinical/data updates: Positive TREMFYA Phase 2b ulcerative colitis response (~80%); ASH 2022 presentations across hematology; Phase 3 PRECISION study shows aprocitentan reduces blood pressure in difficult-to-control hypertension; TREMFYA post-hoc analyses show early efficacy predicts long-term outcomes in psoriatic arthritis; CERENOVUS registry shows positive thrombectomy outcomes.
  - Corporate: CEO Joaquin Duato named Chairman; completion of Abiomed acquisition.

- Administrative note directing readers to SEC filings and investor websites for comprehensive disclosures.

nodes.title: MedTech
nodes.heading: 4.3 MedTech
nodes.start_phrase: MedTech worldwide adjus ted operational sales grew 6.1%*, driven primarily by electrophysiology products in Interventional Solutions, contact lenses in Vision , and wound closure products in General Surgery .
nodes.summary:
- Brief mention of a medication indicated with prednisone for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
- MedTech segment performance: worldwide adjusted operational sales up 6.1%, led by electrophysiology (Interventional Solutions), contact lenses (Vision), and wound closure (General Surgery).
- Investor/legal context: directs readers to SEC filings and company information sites (including resources on talc, prescription opioids, and LTL Management).
- Regulatory milestones: FDA clearance for DePuy Synthes’ TELIGEN System; FDA approval of TECVAYLI (teclistamab-cqyv), the first bispecific T-cell engager for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma; BLA submission to FDA for talquetamab for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.
- Clinical and data updates: Phase 2b TREMFYA (guselkumab) induction study in ulcerative colitis showing ~80% overall clinical response; plans to present hematology pipeline and portfolio data at ASH 2022; Phase 3 PRECISION study shows aprocitentan significantly lowers blood pressure in difficult-to-control hypertension; TREMFYA post-hoc analyses in psoriatic arthritis link early efficacy to sustained long-term outcomes and improved quality of life; CERENOVUS global registry reports positive thrombectomy outcomes in stroke.
- Corporate developments: CEO Joaquin Duato named Chairman of the Board; completion of the Abiomed acquisition.

It reports sales to customers in the U.S., Europe, Western Hemisphere excluding U.S., Asia-Pacific/Africa, International (aggregate), and Worldwide, with percent changes shown as Total, Operational (constant currency), and Currency impact. Key points: Q4 worldwide sales fell 4.4% to $23.7B (operational +0.9%, currency −5.3%), while full-year sales rose 1.3% to $94.9B (operational +6.1%, currency −4.8%). The U.S. grew ~3% in both Q4 and full year with no currency effect. International regions faced substantial FX headwinds: Europe declined 16.0% in Q4 and 0.6% for the year despite strong operational growth (+11% full year); Asia-Pacific/Africa declined in Q4 (−10.0%) with modest operational growth offset by FX. International aggregate was down 11.5% in Q4 and 0.6% for the year, as strong operational growth (+9.1% full year) was more than offset by currency (−9.7%). The Western Hemisphere excluding the U.S. showed mid–single-digit reported growth with double-digit operational gains tempered by FX. A note states percentages use actual, non-rounded figures and may not recalculate precisely.
